# Screen & Notification Dimmer (Night Mode by Bunkwise)

> Screen & Notification Dimmer (formerly listed as "Notification Screen Dimmer" and "Screen Dimmer - Night Mode"; called "Night mode" inside the app) is an Android screen dimmer by Bunkwise Technologies, India. It makes the screen darker than the phone's lowest brightness with an overlay, and with the optional Accessibility service it also dims the status bar, notification shade, keyboard and lock screen. Free to download, no account. A separate free, open-source Windows app also exists.

## Key facts (checked against version 8.0.2, released 21 November 2026)
- Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bunkwise.nightmode (package com.bunkwise.nightmode). Requires Android 8.0 or later. Publisher: Bunkwise Technologies, India. Developer: Madhav Raj.
- How it dims: a dark overlay drawn with "Display over other apps", level 0-100 shown as "% darker than Android's lowest brightness". Capped at 97% opacity so the screen never goes fully black. Quick levels 20, 40, 60, 80 (or your own presets). Default level 40.
- Free: dimming below minimum brightness, bedtime schedule (default 10:30 PM to 6 AM, any days), "Dim for" timer (15, 30, 60 min, until a time, or custom), notification buttons (-10, +10, OFF), on/off Quick Settings tile, emergency off (shake, or Volume Up + Volume Down; both opt-in), usage statistics, "Is everything working?" checker with phone-maker battery tips, light and dark theme.
- Pro: dim the status bar, notification shade and keyboard; edge slider (slide along the left or right screen edge to dim inside any app; also opened from the slider tile); Auto-Dim (Android 11+, raises dimming when a bright page appears; beta); per-app levels; red, amber and custom colour filters; presets; keep dimming after restart.
- Free path to Pro: one short rewarded ad unlocks one Pro feature for 12 hours; three ads within 12 hours unlock all of Pro for 12 hours. Ads only play when the user taps "Watch an ad". Pro can also be bought on Google Play as a weekly subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase, priced by country (weekly: INR 25 in India, USD 0.49 in the US, GBP 0.49 in the UK, EUR 0.49-0.59 in the euro area; lifetime: INR 379, USD 9.99, GBP 8.99, EUR 8.79-10.99; the app shows the local price). New subscribers may get a cheaper first week.
- Permissions: "Display over other apps" (required). Notifications (for the control notification). Accessibility (optional; only for system-area dimming, volume-button escape, per-app levels and Auto-Dim).
- Privacy: no account, no sign-up, dimming works offline. The app includes Google AdMob (optional rewarded ads), Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics, and Microsoft Clarity, behind Google's consent form where required. Full policy: https://bunkwise.in/privacypolicynightmode.html
- Updates: more than 40 code changes since mid-September 2026; latest version 8.0.2 (build 21), released 21 November 2026.
- Not an eye-care or medical app.
- Windows: a separate free, open-source (MIT) Night mode for Windows 10/11 at https://nightmode.bunkwise.in/windows/

# Night Mode: Screen Dimmer for Android

Welcome to the official documentation for Night Mode (Google Play name: Screen & Notification Dimmer), a screen dimmer for Android that makes your display darker than your phone’s lowest brightness setting, including the notification shade and status bar. It was previously listed as Notification Screen Dimmer. It is made by Bunkwise Technologies, India, and the current version is 8.0.2 (21 November 2026).

Get it on Google Play

## What is Night Mode?

Night Mode draws a dark layer over your display so you can dim the screen below your phone’s normal minimum brightness. You choose how dark, and the app shows it as a percentage darker than Android’s lowest brightness. It is built for reading in bed, using a phone next to someone who is asleep, or checking a notification in a dark room without being hit by light.

### Key features

- Dims below minimum brightness - useful in a dark room where the lowest system setting still feels too bright

- Quick levels - 20, 40, 60 and 80 (or your own presets), or drag the slider to any value

- Free bedtime schedule - on at 10:30 PM and off at 6 AM by default; change the times and days

- Dim for - dim for 15, 30 or 60 minutes or until a set time, then back to normal by itself

- Dims the notification bar too - with the optional Accessibility service, also darkens the status bar, notification shade, Quick Settings and keyboard (Pro)

- Edge slider - slide along the screen edge to dim or brighten inside any app (Pro)

- Notification controls - −10, +10 and OFF buttons right in the notification panel (AUTO turns on Auto-Dim)

- Quick Settings tiles - a Night mode on/off tile, plus a Night slider tile in Pro

- Emergency off - shake the phone, or press Volume Up and Volume Down together. Both are off until you turn them on in Settings > Emergency escape

- No account - no sign-up, and dimming works offline. Ads appear only if you choose to watch one to unlock a Pro feature

- Optional Pro - notification-bar dimming, edge slider, Auto-Dim, per-app levels, colour filters, presets and keep-after-restart. One short ad unlocks any Pro feature for 12 hours

## Quick start

- Install Night Mode from Google Play and open it

- Grant “Display over other apps” when asked - this is what lets Night Mode draw its dark layer

- Pick a level - tap 20, 40, 60 or 80, or drag the slider

- Set the schedule - turn on the free bedtime schedule under Automate so it dims by itself every night

- Adjust from anywhere - use the notification buttons, the Quick Settings tile, or the Pro edge slider

- Turn it off any time from the app, the notification or the tile. Turn on shake or Volume Up + Down under Settings > Emergency escape for a blind way out

## Requirements

- An Android phone running Android 8.0 or newer, with Google Play. Auto-Dim needs Android 11 or newer

- Display over other apps permission - required, it draws the dimming layer

- Notifications - for the control notification with its buttons

- Accessibility service - optional, only for dimming the status bar and notification shade, the volume-button emergency shortcut, per-app levels and Auto-Dim

See the User Guide for what each permission is used for.

## Documentation

- User Guide - detailed instructions for all features

- Features - one page per feature, including dimming the notification bar, the edge slider and Auto-Dim

- Alternatives and comparisons - how it compares with Penumbra, Night screen, Darker, Twilight, Extra dim and others

- Guides - phone too bright at night, using it in bed, dimmers that turn off by themselves

- What's new - the changelog

- Dim below minimum brightness - how an overlay dimmer works and how it compares with Extra dim, dark mode and blue light filters

- FAQ - frequently asked questions

- Troubleshooting - solutions to common issues

- Night mode for Windows - the separate free, open-source Windows app

- Privacy Policy - how we handle your data

- Terms of Service - terms and conditions

## Support

Need help? Contact us:

- Email: support@bunkwise.in

- Website: bunkwise.in

# User Guide

Everything Night Mode can do, and how to set it up.

## Getting started

- Install Night Mode from Google Play and open it

- Turn on Display over other apps when asked - Night Mode needs this to draw its dark layer over your screen

- Back on the home screen, pick a level or drag the slider to start dimming

No account, sign-up or login is needed.

## The home screen

The home screen shows everything at a glance:

- Status line - for example “Off · Android’s own minimum” when dimming is off

- Large percentage - how much darker than Android’s lowest brightness the screen is

- Quick levels - 20, 40, 60 and 80, or your first four presets once you have saved some

- Vertical slider - slide towards Darker or Lighter to fine-tune the level

- Help icon - top right, for help inside the app

## Choosing a level

| 
Level | When to use it

| 
20 | A gentle start. Good for the first night or a dim lamp-lit room

| 
40 | Reading in bed with the lights off

| 
60 | A dark room where even the lowest brightness feels harsh

| 
80 | Very dark rooms, or sharing a bed with someone who is asleep

These are suggestions. Every phone panel is different, so move the slider until the screen feels right.

## Slider bar and edge slider (Pro)

A volume-style bar appears over the app you are using, so you can adjust dimming without leaving it. Open it from the Night slider tile, or slide along the screen edge with the edge slider. Both are Pro, or free for 12 hours with one ad. The bar has:

- a vertical slider with the current level at the top

- a moon / power button to switch dimming off

- an AUTO button that turns on Auto-Dim

## The notification

Night Mode shows a notification with the current level and four buttons:

| 
Button | What it does

| 
−10 | Makes the screen 10 points lighter

| 
+10 | Makes the screen 10 points darker

| 
AUTO | Turns Auto-Dim on or off (Pro)

| 
OFF | Turns dimming off straight away

If the notification shows “Tap here: allow Accessibility to dim this panel”, tap it to enable the optional Accessibility service. With Dim notification bar on (Pro, or 12 hours with an ad), Night Mode then dims the notification panel itself.

## Quick Settings tiles

Night Mode adds two tiles to your Quick Settings panel:

- Night mode - one tap to turn dimming on or off, and it shows its current state

- Night slider - opens the dimming bar over whatever you are doing (Pro)

To add them, swipe down twice from the top of the screen, tap the edit (pencil) icon, then drag the Night Mode tiles into your active tiles. The exact steps vary a little between phone makers.

## Emergency off

If the screen ever gets too dark to see, use any of these:

- Shake the phone - off by default; turn it on in Settings > Emergency escape

- Tap OFF in the Night Mode notification

- Switch off the Quick Settings tile

- Press Volume Up and Volume Down together - off by default; turn it on in Emergency escape (needs the optional Accessibility service)

Learn the levels first

Turn on one of the blind escapes first, then start at 20 or 40 and work upwards. You will quickly learn how dark each level is on your phone.

## Permissions

| 
Permission | Required? | What it is used for

| 
Display over other apps | Required | Draws the dark layer over the screen. Dimming cannot work without it

| 
Accessibility service | Optional | Dimming the status bar, notification shade and keyboard; volume-button emergency shortcut; per-app levels; Auto-Dim

Night Mode does not need an account. The dimmer itself runs on the overlay permission alone, so you can leave Accessibility off and everything else still works.

## Free and Pro

| 
 | Free | Pro

| 
Dimming below minimum brightness | Yes | Yes

| 
Quick levels and slider | Yes | Yes

| 
Bedtime schedule and Dim for timer | Yes | Yes

| 
Notification buttons and Quick Settings tiles | Yes | Yes

| 
Emergency off (shake, Volume Up + Down) | Yes | Yes

| 
Edge slider and Night slider tile | 12 h per ad | Yes

| 
Auto-Dim (Android 11+) | 12 h per ad | Yes

| 
Dim the notification bar, status bar and keyboard | 12 h per ad | Yes

| 
Per-app levels | 12 h per ad | Yes

| 
Colour filters, presets, keep after restart | 12 h per ad | Yes

| 
Ads | Only if you tap Watch an ad | None

Pro is bought through Google Play, as a weekly subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase (prices by country are on Free vs Pro), and is tied to your Google account. "12 h per ad" means one short ad unlocks that feature for 12 hours; three ads within 12 hours unlock all of Pro. See Free vs Pro.

## Tips for using it at night

- Combine Night Mode with Android’s dark mode so white apps do not glare

- Lower the system brightness to its minimum first, then add Night Mode on top

- Keep the notification enabled so the OFF button is always one tap away

- Night Mode is a screen dimmer, not a medical device

Last updated: 25 November 2026

# Everything Screen & Notification Dimmer can do

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 4 min read

Short answer
Screen & Notification Dimmer makes an Android screen darker than its lowest brightness setting. The free app covers the essentials: dimming to any level, a bedtime schedule, a timer, notification buttons, a Quick Settings tile and an emergency off. Pro adds the things most overlay dimmers cannot do: dimming the status bar and notification shade, an edge slider, Auto-Dim and a level for each app. You can unlock any Pro feature free for 12 hours by watching one ad.

I started this app because my own phone was still too bright at night with the brightness slider at zero. Most of the features below came from the same kind of small annoyance: the notification shade lighting up the room, a white web page flashing me at 1 AM, or reaching for the app in the dark and not finding it. Each page linked here explains one feature in detail, including its limits.

## Feature list at a glance

| Feature | What it does | Free or Pro

| Dim below minimum brightness | Puts a dark layer over the whole screen, 0 to 100, never fully black | Free
| Bedtime schedule | Turns dimming on and off by itself, 10:30 PM to 6 AM by default | Free
| Dim for a set time | Dims for 15, 30 or 60 minutes, until a time, or any length, then switches off | Free
| Notification controls and tiles | −10, +10 and OFF buttons in the notification, plus an on/off tile | Free
| Emergency off | Shake the phone, or press Volume Up + Volume Down together | Free (opt-in)
| Dim the notification bar | Also darkens the status bar, notification shade, Quick Settings and keyboard | Pro, or 12 h with an ad
| Edge slider | Slide a finger along the screen edge to dim or brighten in any app | Pro, or 12 h with an ad
| Auto-Dim | Dims harder when a bright page appears, eases off on dark pages (Android 11+) | Pro, or 12 h with an ad
| Per-app levels | Remembers a different darkness for each app | Pro, or 12 h with an ad
| Red and amber filters | Tints the dark layer red, amber or a colour you pick | Pro, or 12 h with an ad
| Presets | Save levels you use often and apply them in one tap | Pro, or 12 h with an ad
| Keep dimming after restart | Brings dimming back at your level when the phone boots | Pro, or 12 h with an ad

## What the free version includes

The free version is a complete dimmer, not a trial. It has no time limit, and nothing stops working after a few days. You get the full 0 to 100 range, the quick levels (20, 40, 60 and 80), the bedtime schedule, the timer, the notification buttons, the on/off tile, usage statistics and the "Is everything working?" checker, which finds the battery settings that make some phones kill background apps.

I made the bedtime schedule free on purpose. Most dimmers I looked at put scheduling behind a payment, and it is the one feature that means you never have to open the app at night.

## What Pro adds

Pro is for the parts of the screen and the situations an ordinary overlay misses. A standard "Display over other apps" layer cannot cover the status bar, the pulled-down notification shade or the keyboard, so those stay bright. With Pro and the optional Accessibility service, the dark layer covers them too. Pro also adds the edge slider, Auto-Dim, per-app levels, colour filters, presets and keep-after-restart.

## Using Pro without paying

If you only need a Pro feature now and then, you do not have to buy anything. Tap Watch an ad on a locked feature, and that one feature is unlocked for 12 hours. Watch three ads within 12 hours and all of Pro unlocks for 12 hours. Ads only play when you tap that button yourself. They never appear while you are dimming or reading. The Free vs Pro guide explains it step by step.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Screen & Notification Dimmer free?

Yes. Dimming below minimum brightness, the bedtime schedule, the timer, the notification buttons, the tile and emergency off are free with no time limit. Pro features can be bought, or unlocked for 12 hours by watching a short ad.

### Which Android versions does it support?

Android 8.0 (Oreo) and newer. Auto-Dim needs Android 11 or newer, because it uses a screenshot API that older versions do not have.

### Does it need root?

No. It uses the standard "Display over other apps" permission, plus the optional Accessibility service for the status bar and other system areas.

# Dim the notification bar, status bar and keyboard on Android

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 4 min read

Short answer
Ordinary overlay dimmers cannot draw over the status bar, the pulled-down notification shade, Quick Settings or the keyboard, so those parts stay bright. Screen & Notification Dimmer can dim them as well. Turn on Dim notification bar in the app and allow its optional Accessibility service; the dark layer then sits above the system areas too. It is a Pro feature, and you can unlock it free for 12 hours by watching one ad.

This is the feature the app is named after. If you have used an overlay dimmer before, you know the moment: the screen is nicely dark, then you pull down the notification shade to check a message and a bright white panel lights up the whole room. In a dark bedroom that is the brightest thing you see all night.

## Why most dimmers can't reach the notification shade

Android lets apps draw over other apps with the "Display over other apps" permission (its technical name is TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY). For security, Android keeps that kind of window below the system's own surfaces. The status bar, the notification shade, Quick Settings, the keyboard and the lock screen are all drawn above it, and some screens, such as parts of the Settings app, hide ordinary overlays altogether. So an overlay dimmer, however dark it is, has a bright hole exactly where your notifications appear.

There is one window type that sits higher: the Accessibility overlay. Only an app running an Accessibility service may use it. That is the route Screen & Notification Dimmer takes when you switch this feature on.

## What gets dimmed

| Screen area | Normal overlay | With Dim notification bar

| Apps, home screen, videos | Dimmed | Dimmed
| Status bar (clock, battery icons) | Stays bright | Dimmed
| Pulled-down notification shade | Stays bright | Dimmed
| Quick Settings panel | Stays bright | Dimmed
| Keyboard | Often stays bright | Dimmed
| Lock screen | Not covered | Dimmed
| Settings app screens that hide overlays | Not covered | Dimmed

## How to turn it on

- Open Screen & Notification Dimmer and turn dimming on.

- Find Dim notification bar ("Also darkens the status bar and the pulled-down shade") and switch it on. If you do not have Pro, tap Watch an ad to unlock it for 12 hours.

- The app explains what the Accessibility service does, then opens Android's Accessibility settings. Go to Downloaded apps (or Installed apps), choose Night mode - better dimming and allow it.

- Pull down the shade. It should now be as dark as the rest of the screen.

The notification itself also nudges you: if the service is off, it shows "Tap here: allow Accessibility to dim this panel too".

Some phones add a step

On Android 13 and newer, an app installed from outside Google Play may show "Restricted setting" when you try to allow Accessibility. Installed from Play, you normally won't see this. On Xiaomi, Vivo and Oppo phones the Accessibility list can be under "Downloaded apps" or "Installed services".

## What the Accessibility service can and cannot see

Accessibility is a powerful permission, so it is fair to ask what it is used for. In this app the service draws the dark layer over system areas. If you switch the related features on, it also watches for the Volume Up + Volume Down emergency combination, notes which app is in front for per-app levels, and, for Auto-Dim, measures how bright the screen is from a tiny downscaled screenshot that is thrown away straight after. It does not read the text on your screen, record what you type, or control other apps. Each of those extras has its own switch. The full details are in the privacy policy, section 1.

## How it compares with other apps

A few dimmers offer something similar, usually as a paid extra. According to their Google Play listings, Night screen calls it "Advanced dimming" in its premium tier, Super Dim extends its filter over system areas in premium, and Darker sells "Darken navigation bar" as a paid feature. Plain overlay apps such as Dimmer: Night Screen Overlay do not mention covering the status bar at all. What is different here is that you can try it free for 12 hours with one ad before deciding whether it is worth paying for.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why is my notification panel still bright when the dimmer is on?

Because ordinary overlays are drawn below the notification shade. To dim it, an app needs an Accessibility overlay. In Screen & Notification Dimmer, turn on Dim notification bar and allow the "Night mode - better dimming" Accessibility service.

### Can I dim the keyboard on Android?

Yes. With Dim notification bar on and the Accessibility service allowed, the keyboard is dimmed along with the rest of the screen.

### Is Dim notification bar free?

It is a Pro feature. You can unlock it for 12 hours by watching one short ad, as many times as you like, or buy Pro to keep it on permanently.

### Does it work on Samsung, Xiaomi and OnePlus?

Yes, it uses a standard Android window type. The only difference between brands is where the Accessibility switch sits in Settings.

- Screen dimmer app vs Android's Extra dim
- Android screen dimmer apps compared (2026)

# Edge slider: change the darkness by sliding along the screen edge

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
The edge slider lets you change how dark the screen is without opening Screen & Notification Dimmer. Slide a finger down the right (or left) edge of the screen to make it darker, or up to make it brighter, inside any app. A volume-style bar shows the level, then hides itself. Tap the moon icon on the bar to switch dimming off. It is a Pro feature, and one ad unlocks it for 12 hours.

Dimming is not a set-and-forget thing. A dark film scene needs less, a white web page needs more, and you only find out once you are already in the app. Going back to the dimmer every time breaks what you were doing, so I wanted the control to be where your thumb already is, the same way the volume bar appears when you press a button.

## How the edge slider works

- Slide down along the edge for darker, slide up for brighter.

- The bar appears at the edge with the current level, follows your finger, and hides itself after a moment. A tap anywhere else hides it at once.

- Tap the moon icon at the foot of the bar to turn dimming off.

- AUTO under the bar switches on Auto-Dim.

- Choose the right edge or the left edge. Left-handed users usually prefer the left.

- The bar and its handle are kept above the dark layer, so they are never dimmed themselves and you can always see them.

The Night slider Quick Settings tile opens the same bar. That helps if you would rather start from the pull-down panel than from the edge.

## How to set it up

- Open Screen & Notification Dimmer and find Edge slider on the Dim screen.

- Switch it on. Without Pro, tap Watch an ad to unlock it for 12 hours.

- Pick Right edge or Left edge under Settings > Control from anywhere.

- Open any app and slide along that edge.

## Will it get in the way of the back gesture?

Android's back gesture is a sideways swipe in from the edge, while the edge slider follows a movement along the edge, up or down. The handle is a thin strip, so an ordinary back swipe still works. If an app of yours relies heavily on edge swipes (some drawing and reading apps do), move the slider to the other side.

## Is this common in other dimmers?

Not that I found. I read the Google Play listings of the dimmers that come up most often in searches (Penumbra, Night screen, Darker, Super Dim and others). They offer sliders inside the app, in the notification or in a tile, but none of them describes an edge gesture that works inside other apps. If that changes, I will update this page.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I change screen dimming without opening the app?

Use the edge slider (slide along the screen edge), the −10 and +10 buttons on the notification, or the Night slider tile in Quick Settings.

### Can I put the edge slider on the left side?

Yes. Choose Left edge in the app's settings.

### Does the edge slider turn dimming on?

Sliding only changes the level. Dragging it all the way up makes the layer clear but does not switch the service off. To turn dimming off, tap the moon icon on the bar.

# Auto-Dim: a dimmer that reacts to what is on screen

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
Auto-Dim changes the dimming level by itself based on how bright the content on your screen is. When a white page or a bright reel appears, it dims more. When you are back on a dark page, it eases off. It needs Android 11 or newer and the optional Accessibility service. It is a Pro feature, still marked beta, and one ad unlocks it for 12 hours.

At night the problem is often not the average brightness, it is the jumps. You are scrolling a dark feed at a comfortable level, then the next video opens on a white background and it feels like a camera flash. People call it a "flashbang". A fixed dimming level cannot help, because the level that is right for the dark feed is far too bright for the white page.

## How Auto-Dim works

While dimming and Auto-Dim are both on, the app takes a screenshot through Android's Accessibility screenshot API several times a second. It shrinks each one to a tiny low-resolution grid and works out one number: how bright the content is. Bright content raises the dimming, dark content lowers it. The image is processed in memory and thrown away immediately. It is never saved, never written to storage and never sent anywhere.

The readout in the app shows what it sees, for example "Following the screen · content is 72% bright now".

## Settings you can adjust

| Setting | What it changes

| Strength | How far the level moves between dark and bright content
| Reaction speed: Gentle, Medium or Fast | How quickly it responds. Gentle avoids flicker during fast scrolling; Fast catches sudden flashes sooner

## How it differs from auto-brightness

Android's adaptive brightness and apps such as Lux or Super Dim's automatic mode respond to the room, using the light sensor. In a dark bedroom the room barely changes, so the sensor has nothing to react to. Auto-Dim responds to the content, which is what actually changes when a bright page opens. The two work well together: let the system handle the room, and let Auto-Dim handle the screen.

## Limits, honestly

- Android 11 or newer only. The screenshot API it relies on does not exist before Android 11.

- Battery. It samples many times a second, so it uses more battery than plain dimming. The app says this up front, and how much depends on the phone.

- Protected content. Some apps (banking apps and DRM video) block screenshots. Android may not hand over a usable screenshot there, so Auto-Dim may not react inside those apps.

- Beta. I am still tuning it on different phones. If it misbehaves on yours, write to support@bunkwise.in with your phone model.

## How to turn it on

- Go to the Automate tab and switch on Auto-Dim. Without Pro, tap Watch an ad for a 12-hour unlock.

- Allow the "Night mode - better dimming" Accessibility service when asked.

- Set Strength and Reaction speed, then open a mixed app such as a browser to see it respond.

You can also toggle it with the AUTO button on the notification or under the edge slider.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there an app that dims bright white pages automatically?

Yes. Auto-Dim in Screen & Notification Dimmer raises the dimming when the content on screen turns bright and lowers it when the content is dark. It needs Android 11 or newer.

### Does Auto-Dim record my screen?

No. It reduces each screenshot to a single brightness number in memory and discards the image immediately. Nothing is saved or sent.

### Why does Auto-Dim not react in my banking app?

Apps that block screenshots may not give Android's screenshot API a usable image, so Auto-Dim may not react there. Give those apps a fixed per-app level instead.

## Related pages

- Dim the notification bar, status bar and keyboard on Android
- Per-app levels: each app keeps its own darkness
- Watching videos and reels in a dark room
- Overlay dimming vs real brightness: what actually happens

# Control dimming from the notification and Quick Settings

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
While dimming is on, Screen & Notification Dimmer shows a notification with four buttons: −10 (lighter), +10 (darker), AUTO (Auto-Dim) and OFF. Pull down the shade and tap; you never need to open the app. There is also a Night mode on/off tile for Quick Settings. The notification buttons and the on/off tile are free.

Most of the time you want to change dimming while doing something else, such as reading or watching. The notification is the one place that is always a swipe away, so the controls belong there.

## The notification buttons

| Button | What it does | Free?

| −10 | Makes the screen 10 points lighter | Free
| +10 | Makes the screen 10 points darker | Free
| AUTO | Turns Auto-Dim on or off | Pro, or 12 h with an ad
| OFF | Switches dimming off at once | Free

The title shows the level, for example "Dimming on - 40%". You can hide the buttons in the app's settings if you would rather have a plain status notification.

Keep notifications allowed

On Android 13 and newer, apps must ask before showing notifications. If you tapped "Don't allow", the buttons can't appear. Turn notifications back on in the app ("Turn on notifications to dim from the shade") or in Android Settings > Apps > Night mode > Notifications. The notification is also the most reliable way to switch dimming off, so it is worth keeping.

## Quick Settings tiles

- Night mode toggles dimming at your current level and shows it, for example "On · 40%". Free.

- Night slider opens the volume-style dimming bar over whatever you are doing, the same bar as the edge slider. Pro, or 12 hours with an ad.

To add them: swipe down twice from the top of the screen, tap the edit pencil, then drag "Night mode" and "Night slider" up into your active tiles. On Samsung the edit button sits behind the three-dot menu, and on Xiaomi HyperOS it is the edit icon in the Control Centre.

## Will the notification bother me?

It only shows while dimming is on, because Android needs a visible notification to keep the dimming service alive. Other notifications from the app are rare and never break through Do Not Disturb.

The panel you pull down to reach these buttons is bright by default. If that bothers you, see how to dim the notification bar itself.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I adjust dimming without opening the app?

Yes. Use the −10 and +10 buttons on the notification, the Night mode tile in Quick Settings, or the edge slider.

### Why did the dimmer notification disappear?

It only shows while dimming is on. If dimming is on and there is no notification, notifications for the app are probably blocked. Allow them in Android Settings > Apps > Night mode > Notifications.

### Is there a screen dimmer Quick Settings tile?

Yes. Screen & Notification Dimmer adds a Night mode on/off tile (free) and a Night slider tile (Pro) to Quick Settings.

# Emergency off: getting your screen back when it is too dark

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
If the screen is too dark to see, you can turn Screen & Notification Dimmer off without looking. Shake the phone, or press Volume Up and Volume Down together. Both are off by default and switched on in Settings > Emergency escape. The OFF button on the notification and the Quick Settings tile also always work. The dark layer is also capped, so the screen never goes completely black.

Every dimmer has the same nightmare case. You drag the slider too far, the screen goes nearly black, and now you can't see the button that would fix it. I wanted at least one way out that needs no eyesight at all.

## Every way to switch it off

| Method | Needs to see the screen? | Default

| Press Volume Up + Volume Down together | No | Off, turn on in Emergency escape (needs the Accessibility service)
| Shake the phone firmly | No | Off, turn on in Emergency escape or from the Shake tile on Home
| Tap OFF on the notification | A little | Always available
| Tap the Night mode Quick Settings tile | A little | Always available
| Turn off in the app | Yes | Always available

When an escape fires, the app tells you what happened ("You pressed Volume Up + Down together") so it never looks like a crash.

## Why both are off by default

Shake used to be on from the start. The trouble is that a phone carried in a pocket or bag gets shaken too, and the dimming would vanish for no visible reason. Pressing both volume keys also happens by accident, for example when you grab the phone in bed. A dimmer that switches itself off unasked feels broken, so both escapes are now opt-in. Turn on whichever suits you the first time you set the app up.

## Adjusting the shake

Shake has a strength setting. If it fires while you walk, make it firmer; if it never fires, make it lighter. The volume combination is more precise and works inside any app, so it is the better choice if you can allow the Accessibility service.

## A safety cap on darkness

Even at 100 the dark layer is not fully opaque. It stops at 97%, so on most phones you can still make out the screen in a dark room. That is deliberate. A fully black overlay would look exactly like a phone that has switched off.

## Is this unusual?

Shake-to-disable is fairly common. Penumbra and Super Dim both list it. The volume-button combination is less common. I didn't find it in the listings of the other dimmers I compared, and it is the one I would pick, because it works without any guesswork.

## Frequently asked questions

### My screen is too dark to see. How do I turn the dimmer off?

Press Volume Up and Volume Down together, or shake the phone, if you enabled those. Otherwise pull down from the top of the screen and tap OFF on the dimmer notification or tap the Night mode tile. Restarting the phone also clears the overlay, unless keep-after-restart is on.

### Is shake to turn off on by default?

No. In current versions both shake and the volume-button escape are off until you switch them on under Settings > Emergency escape.

### Can the screen go completely black?

No. The dark layer is capped at 97% opacity, so the screen stays faintly visible.

# A free bedtime schedule that dims the screen for you

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
Screen & Notification Dimmer can turn dimming on and off by itself every night. Open the Automate tab, switch on Night auto-dim, and choose the times and days. The default is 10:30 PM to 6:00 AM, every day. The schedule is free, with no ads and no trial.

If you have to remember to switch the dimmer on, you will forget on the nights you need it. A schedule fixes that: the screen is already dark when you pick the phone up in bed, and back to normal in the morning.

## How to set it up

- Open the app and go to Automate > Schedule.

- Switch on Night auto-dim.

- Set the on time and the off time. The app shows how long that is, for example "Dimming for 7h 30m a night, every day".

- Under Repeat on, choose every day, weekdays, weekends or any set of days.

The 24-hour strip at the top shows the dimmed window, so overnight times such as 11 PM to 7 AM are easy to check.

## How accurate is the timing?

The schedule fires within a couple of minutes of the time you set, even when the phone is in Doze. To-the-second timing would need Android's exact alarm permission, and I chose not to ask for it, because a dimmer doesn't need it. If you open the phone exactly at 10:30, give it a minute.

If you set the on and off times to the same value, the app warns you that nothing will happen. If no days are ticked, it says the schedule will never fire.

## Making it reliable on Xiaomi, Samsung and others

Some phone makers stop background apps more aggressively than stock Android, and that can stop a schedule from firing. Set the app's battery usage to Unrestricted and, on Xiaomi, Vivo and Oppo, allow Autostart. The built-in "Is everything working?" page checks this for you. The guide to dimmers turning off by themselves covers each brand.

## Free here, paid elsewhere

I checked how other popular dimmers handle this on their Play listings. Night screen lists its "Auto start & stop timer" under premium, and Darker lists "Auto-On & Auto-Off" among its paid features. Penumbra is one that also has a free schedule. Here it is free because it is the feature that matters most for a bedtime dimmer.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I make my Android screen dim automatically at night?

Install Screen & Notification Dimmer, open Automate > Schedule, switch on Night auto-dim and set your times. It is free.

### Can I schedule dimming only on weekdays?

Yes. Under Repeat on, choose weekdays, weekends, or any individual days.

### Why did the schedule start a minute late?

Android batches background alarms to save battery, so the schedule fires within a couple of minutes of the set time. The app deliberately does not request the exact-alarm permission.

# Dim for a while: a sleep timer for your screen

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
Tap Dim for in Screen & Notification Dimmer and pick how long: 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, until a specific time, a custom length, or until you turn it off. The screen dims at your level, then returns to normal by itself when the time is up. The app shows the time left on the home screen. It is free.

A timer is for the times you know you will only need the dark for a while: reading a few chapters before sleep, a film in a dark room, or a night feed with a baby where you want the phone back to normal afterwards.

## Options

| Choice | What happens

| 15 min, 30 min, 1 hour | Dims now, turns off after that long
| Until a time | Dims until the clock time shown, for example "until 11:45 PM"
| Some other length | Type any number of minutes
| Until I turn it off | Plain dimming with no timer

While a timer runs, the status line says "Back to normal at 11:45 PM" and a countdown shows the time left.

## Timer or schedule?

Use the bedtime schedule for the same hours every night. Use Dim for for one-off sessions. 

Several other dimmers have a timer too. Penumbra offers 15, 30 or 60 minutes from a long-press, for example. The "until a time" option is the one people tend to miss elsewhere.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a screen dimmer turn off by itself after some time?

Yes. Use Dim for in Screen & Notification Dimmer and pick 15, 30 or 60 minutes, a clock time, or a custom length.

### Does the timer keep running if I close the app?

Yes. It runs in the dimming service, so it works with the app closed or the screen off.

# Per-app levels: each app keeps its own darkness

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
Per-app profiles let Screen & Notification Dimmer switch the dimming level automatically when you open a particular app. For example, YouTube at 70, your reading app at 30 and Maps at 0, while everything else stays at your usual level. It uses the optional Accessibility service only to know which app is in front. It is a Pro feature, and one ad unlocks it for 12 hours.

One level rarely fits everything. Video apps in a dark room want a lot of dimming. A white e-book page wants some. Maps in the car at night may need none at all, or you won't read the street names. Without per-app levels you end up moving the slider every time you switch apps.

## How to set it up

- Go to Automate > Per-app profiles and switch it on (or Watch an ad for 12 hours).

- Tap Choose an app, search for it, and set the level it should dim to.

- Allow the "Night mode - better dimming" Accessibility service if you haven't already. It is the same permission the volume-button escape uses, so there is nothing extra to grant.

The page then shows a summary like "3 apps set · everything else stays at 40%".

## What it can see

The service only notes the package name of the app in front, such as com.google.android.youtube, and only in memory. It never sees what is on the screen or what you type, and it keeps no history of the apps you used.

## Ideas that work well

| App type | Suggested level | Why

| Video and reels | 60–80 | Dark rooms, bright content
| E-books and news | 30–50 | White pages, long sessions
| Maps and navigation | 0–20 | You need to read it at a glance
| Camera and gallery | 0 | Judging photos needs true brightness
| Banking and UPI apps | 0 | Some block taps while an overlay is on

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I set different screen brightness for different apps on Android?

Android itself does not offer this, but Screen & Notification Dimmer's per-app profiles set a dimming level for each app and switch automatically when you open it.

### Does per-app dimming read my screen?

No. It only knows the name of the app in front, in memory. It does not see screen content or keystrokes.

# Red, amber and custom colour filters

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
Screen & Notification Dimmer can tint its dark layer instead of using plain black. Pick Red night light, Amber or a custom colour, and the screen becomes darker and warmer in one step. Black is free. The tints are part of Pro, and one ad unlocks them for 12 hours. Custom colours are automatically kept dark enough to read.

Some people want less light, and some want warmer light. Many want both at bedtime. Android's Night Light warms the colours but cannot go below minimum brightness, and most blue-light filter apps are the other way round. The filter here adds the colour to the dimming layer itself, so you get both from one control.

## The filters

| Filter | What it looks like | Good for

| Black | Just darker, colours unchanged | Films, photos, anything where colour matters. Free
| Red night light | Deep red tint | Very dark rooms, astronomy, keeping the room as dark as possible
| Amber | Warm, like a bedside lamp | Reading and scrolling in bed
| Custom colour | Any tint you pick, auto-darkened to stay readable | Matching your own taste

## Filter or Android's Night Light?

You can use both. Night Light changes the colour temperature at the system level. This filter adds a tinted dark layer on top. Together they give a warmer image than either alone. If your goal is mainly warmth with only a little dimming, a dedicated filter such as Twilight may suit you better. If your goal is darkness first, a dimmer with a tint is the better fit. The dimmer vs blue light filter page goes through the difference.

A note on claims: I am not going to tell you a red filter improves your sleep or protects your eyes. This is a screen dimmer, not a medical device. Plenty of people simply find warm, dim light more comfortable at night, and that is what the filter is for.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a red screen filter app for Android?

Yes. Screen & Notification Dimmer has a Red night light filter that tints the dimming layer red, alongside Amber and custom colours.

### Does the colour filter work below minimum brightness?

Yes. The tint is part of the dimming layer, so the screen gets darker and warmer at the same time.

# Android screen dimmer apps compared (2026)

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
Any overlay dimmer will make an Android screen darker than its lowest brightness. The real differences are in the details: whether it can dim the notification shade and status bar, whether the schedule is free, how you switch it off in the dark, and whether it has ads. Screen & Notification Dimmer is the pick if you want the notification bar dimmed, an edge slider, content-aware Auto-Dim and a free schedule. Penumbra is a good pick if you want no ads at all, and Twilight if you mainly want a blue light filter.

A note on bias

I make Screen & Notification Dimmer, so read this knowing that. Every fact about the other app comes from its own Google Play listing, checked on 25 November 2026. I have not claimed anything the listing does not say. If something is out of date, email support@bunkwise.in and I will correct it.

These are the dimmers that come up most often when people, or AI assistants, search Google Play for "screen dimmer", "low brightness" or "night screen". I read each listing in full and noted what it actually claims. Then I wrote one page per app with a side-by-side comparison and a section on when you should pick that app instead of mine.

## Quick comparison

| App | Best for | Ads (Play label) | Downloads | Last updated

| Screen & Notification Dimmer | Dimming the notification bar; edge slider; free schedule; Auto-Dim | Optional rewarded ads only | 1K+ | 21 Nov 2026

| Night Screen: Ultra Dim Mode | RGB colour filters, sunset schedule | No | 500K+ | 25 May 2026
| Screen Dimmer – OLED Saver | OLED and PWM-focused users | No | 100K+ | 28 May 2026
| Lux Auto Brightness | No longer listed on Google Play | – | – | –

## How to choose a screen dimmer

- Does the notification shade stay bright? Plain overlays can't cover it. If pulling the shade down at night bothers you, choose an app that uses an Accessibility overlay for system areas (here is why).

- Can you switch it off blind? Look for shake or a hardware-button escape, and a level cap so the screen can't go fully black.

- Is the schedule free? It is the feature that makes a dimmer effortless, and several apps charge for it.

- Is it still maintained? Android changes overlay rules almost every year. An app last updated long ago is more likely to break on a new phone.

- What permissions does it want? Only "Display over other apps" is needed for basic dimming. Accessibility should be optional and explained.

It depends on what you need. Screen & Notification Dimmer is strongest if you want the notification shade and status bar dimmed, an edge slider, Auto-Dim and a free schedule. Penumbra suits people who want no ads at all. Twilight suits people who mainly want a blue light filter.

Screen & Notification Dimmer (Pro, or 12 hours free with an ad) and, according to their listings, the premium tiers of Night screen and Super Dim. They all use an Accessibility overlay.

Yes. Screen & Notification Dimmer and Penumbra both list a free schedule.

# Penumbra – Screen Dimmer vs Screen & Notification Dimmer

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
Penumbra is a well-made, free dimmer with no ads and no paywall. Its listing also highlights Tasker control, TalkBack support and seven languages. Screen & Notification Dimmer is the alternative if you want things Penumbra does not list: dimming the status bar and notification shade, an edge slider inside any app, content-aware Auto-Dim, per-app levels and a Volume Up + Down emergency off. If "no ads, ever" matters most to you, Penumbra is the honest choice.

A note on bias

I make Screen & Notification Dimmer, so read this knowing that. Every fact about the other app comes from its own Google Play listing, checked on 25 November 2026. I have not claimed anything the listing does not say. If something is out of date, email support@bunkwise.in and I will correct it.

## About Penumbra

| Listing detail | As shown on Google Play (25 November 2026)

| Title | Penumbra - Screen Dimmer
| Ads / in-app purchases | Listing says: "Free, no ads, no paywall"
| Downloads | 1K+
| Updated | 21 November 2026

According to its listing, Penumbra has a dial that goes below the system minimum, Extra Dim integration for going deeper, a continuous warm (amber) slider, a Quick Settings tile, a notification toggle, presets that save dim and warmth together, an auto schedule, an auto-off timer (15, 30 or 60 minutes), start on boot, shake to disable, Tasker and Automate broadcasts, and full TalkBack support. Its privacy section says it has no ads and no advertising ID, with anonymous crash and usage reporting only.

## Where Penumbra is strong

- Completely free, with no ads or paywall at all.

- Automation through Tasker and Automate intents. I don't offer this yet.

- Accessibility and languages: TalkBack support and seven languages are listed.

- A clear note in the listing about overlays not saving battery on LCD screens, which I appreciate.

## Where Screen & Notification Dimmer is different

- The notification shade and status bar get dimmed. Penumbra's listing describes an overlay over apps and doesn't mention system areas. How this works.

- Edge slider: change darkness by sliding along the screen edge, inside any app. Details.

- Auto-Dim reacts to bright pages as they appear. Details.

- Per-app levels, so YouTube can be darker than your reading app.

- Volume Up + Volume Down emergency off, as well as shake.

- Notification buttons for −10 and +10, not only a toggle.

# Lux Auto Brightness alternative: what to use now

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
When I checked on 25 November 2026, Lux Auto Brightness's old Google Play address (com.vito.lux) returned "Not Found". If you used Lux to go below minimum brightness, any overlay dimmer such as Screen & Notification Dimmer does that. For automatic adjustment, Android's own adaptive brightness handles the room, and Screen & Notification Dimmer's Auto-Dim handles bright content on screen. For warm colours, use Night Light or a colour filter.

A note on bias

I make Screen & Notification Dimmer, so read this knowing that. Every fact about the other app comes from its own Google Play listing, checked on 25 November 2026. I have not claimed anything the listing does not say. If something is out of date, email support@bunkwise.in and I will correct it.

## What happened to Lux?

Lux was a well-known brightness app for Android that took over from the system auto-brightness, learned from your adjustments and could dim below the minimum. I can't confirm why it is gone, only that its listing no longer loads on Google Play. If you still have an old copy installed, it may keep working, but an app that no longer gets updates can break on newer Android versions, which change overlay and background rules regularly.

## Replacing each thing Lux did

| What you used Lux for | What to use now

| Going darker than minimum brightness | An overlay dimmer: Screen & Notification Dimmer, Penumbra or Night screen
| Adjusting to the room automatically | Android's Adaptive brightness (Settings > Display). It learns from your slider changes too
| Avoiding bright flashes from white pages | Screen & Notification Dimmer Auto-Dim, which follows on-screen content (Android 11+)
| Night-time profile at fixed hours | Screen & Notification Dimmer free bedtime schedule
| Warm colour at night | Android's Night Light, or a red or amber filter
| Per-app brightness | Screen & Notification Dimmer per-app levels

## Why I'd pair two tools rather than one

Lux mixed two jobs: reading the light sensor and dimming the screen. Since Android 9, the system's adaptive brightness learns from you, so it now does the sensor job well. What it still can't do is go below the hardware minimum, or react when the content on screen suddenly turns white. Those are the gaps a dimmer fills. Let Android set the backlight, and let the dimmer handle the last stretch in the dark.

## Side by side with today's options

| | Screen & Notification Dimmer | Android adaptive brightness

| Below minimum brightness | Yes | No
| Reacts to room light | No (use adaptive brightness) | Yes
| Reacts to bright content | Yes, Auto-Dim (Pro, Android 11+) | No
| Schedule | Yes, free | No
| Dims status bar and shade | Yes (Pro) | Backlight only

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Lux Auto Brightness still on Google Play?

When checked on 25 November 2026, its Play address com.vito.lux returned "Not Found".

### What is the best Lux alternative?

Use Android's adaptive brightness for the room, plus an overlay dimmer such as Screen & Notification Dimmer for going below minimum, schedules and Auto-Dim.

- Android screen dimmer apps compared (2026)
- Auto-Dim: a dimmer that reacts to what is on screen
- Overlay dimming vs real brightness: what actually happens

# Twilight vs Screen & Notification Dimmer: filter or dimmer?

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
Twilight and Screen & Notification Dimmer solve different problems. Twilight is a blue light filter: it warms the screen gradually, following your local sunset and sunrise. Screen & Notification Dimmer is a dimmer: it makes the screen darker than its minimum, with an optional red or amber tint. If your screen feels too bright, choose the dimmer. If it feels too blue, choose Twilight. Some people use both.

A note on bias

I make Screen & Notification Dimmer, so read this knowing that. Every fact about the other app comes from its own Google Play listing, checked on 25 November 2026. I have not claimed anything the listing does not say. If something is out of date, email support@bunkwise.in and I will correct it.

## About Twilight

| Listing detail | As shown on Google Play (25 November 2026)

| Title | Twilight: Blue light filter
| Rating | 4.6 from about 452,000 ratings
| Downloads | 10M+
| Updated | 29 September 2026

According to its listing, Twilight filters blue light after sunset with a soft red filter whose strength follows the sun cycle for your location. It can lower the backlight below the normal controls, tints dark areas such as the status bar, filters notifications and the lock screen with an optional Accessibility service, syncs with Wear OS, supports Tasker, and can control Philips Hue lights. It uses location to find sunset times.

## Where Twilight is strong

- Sunset-aware timing that shifts through the year without you touching it.

- A huge, long-standing user base and a high rating.

- Extras: Wear OS, Philips Hue and Tasker.

## Where Screen & Notification Dimmer is different

- Darkness first. A plain black layer that keeps colours true, useful for films and photos, with tints as an option.

- Edge slider and notification buttons to change darkness quickly, in the moment.

- Auto-Dim reacts to bright content, not to the time of day.

- Emergency off by shake or volume buttons.

- No location permission. The schedule uses the times you set.

## Side by side

| | Screen & Notification Dimmer | Twilight

| Dims below minimum brightness | Yes, 0–100, capped at 97% so never fully black | Can lower backlight below the normal range (per listing)
| Dims status bar and notification shade | Yes (Pro, or 12 h free with an ad) | Yes, notifications and lock screen via Accessibility
| Schedule | Yes, free | Follows local sunset and sunrise
| Timer | Yes, free (15/30/60 min, until a time, custom) | Not mentioned in listing
| Notification controls | Yes, free: −10, +10, AUTO, OFF | Not mentioned in listing
| Quick Settings tile | Yes, free on/off tile; slider tile in Pro | Not mentioned in listing
| Edge slider in any app | Yes (Pro, or 12 h free with an ad) | Not mentioned in listing
| Automatic dimming | Auto-Dim reacts to screen content (Pro, Android 11+) | Not mentioned in listing
| Per-app levels | Yes (Pro, or 12 h free with an ad) | Not mentioned in listing
| Colour filter | Red, amber, custom (Pro); black free | Red/blue-light filter, the main feature
| Emergency off | Shake or Volume Up + Down (opt-in), plus notification and tile | Not mentioned in listing
| Ads | Only rewarded ads you choose to watch | Not mentioned in listing
| Last updated on Play | 21 November 2026 (version 8.0.2) | 29 September 2026
| Downloads on Play | 1K+ (new app) | 10M+

## Using both

A sensible night setup is Twilight (or Android's Night Light) for warmth and Screen & Notification Dimmer for darkness. Keep the dimmer's filter on Black when you do, so the two tints don't stack into something too red to read.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a blue light filter the same as a screen dimmer?

No. A blue light filter changes colour; a dimmer reduces brightness. Twilight is mainly a filter; Screen & Notification Dimmer is mainly a dimmer.

### Can I use Twilight and a dimmer together?

Yes. Use Twilight for warmth and the dimmer for darkness, with the dimmer's colour set to Black.

# Screen dimmer app vs Android's Extra dim

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
Android's Extra dim (the name on Pixel and Samsung phones; the underlying Android setting is “Reduce Bright Colors”) lowers the screen beyond the normal slider at the system level. A dimmer app such as Screen & Notification Dimmer adds a dark layer on top. Extra dim is built in and covers everything, but it has one fixed strength range and no schedule on many phones. A dimmer app adds finer control, schedules, notification buttons and an emergency off. Using both together gives the darkest screen.

## What Extra dim is

Google added Extra dim in Android 12. It lives under Settings > Accessibility (sometimes Settings > Display), with an intensity slider and a Quick Settings tile. Samsung has its own "Extra dim" in One UI. Some phone makers don't include it at all, and on others it is hidden. How strong it is depends on the phone.

## Comparison

| | Extra dim (built in) | Screen & Notification Dimmer

| Goes below minimum brightness | Yes | Yes
| Available on every phone | No, depends on maker and Android version | Android 8.0 and newer
| Covers status bar and shade | Yes | Yes with Dim notification bar (Pro)
| Fine control | One intensity slider in Settings | 0–100 slider, quick levels, notification ±10, edge slider
| Schedule | Not on most phones | Yes, free
| Timer | No | Yes, free
| Per-app levels | No | Yes (Pro)
| Reacts to bright content | No | Auto-Dim (Pro, Android 11+)
| Emergency off | Tile or Settings | Shake, Volume Up + Down, notification, tile
| Colour tint | No | Red, amber, custom (Pro)

## Use both for the darkest result

Extra dim and an overlay stack. Turn Extra dim on at a moderate strength, then use the dimmer for fine control on top. That way you get the darkness of both, plus a schedule and quick buttons.

## Does Extra dim save battery?

Extra dim usually lowers the actual output of the panel, so it can save a little battery, especially on LCDs. An overlay mostly darkens the image, which on OLED screens also means darker pixels and less power, but on LCD the backlight stays the same. See overlay vs real brightness.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Android's Extra dim better than a screen dimmer app?

Neither is strictly better. Extra dim is built in; a dimmer app adds schedules, timers, notification controls and an emergency off. Together they give the darkest screen.

### Why can't I find Extra dim on my phone?

It depends on the phone maker and Android version. Search Settings for "Extra dim" or "Reduce bright colours". If it is missing, a dimmer app does the same job.

### Can I use Extra dim and a dimmer app together?

Yes. They stack, which makes the screen darker than either alone.

# Screen dimmer vs blue light filter: darker or warmer?

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
A screen dimmer reduces how much light the screen gives off. A blue light filter (Android's Night Light, Eye Comfort Shield on Samsung, or apps such as Twilight) shifts the colours towards orange. If the screen feels glaring in a dark room, you want a dimmer. If it feels cold and white, you want a filter. Many people use both at night.

## The difference

| | Screen dimmer | Blue light filter / Night Light

| Changes | Brightness | Colour temperature
| Goes below minimum brightness | Yes | No (a filter alone does not)
| Keeps colours accurate | Yes, with a black layer | No, everything turns orange
| Built into Android | Extra dim, on some phones | Night Light, on almost all phones
| Best for | Dark rooms, sleeping partners, reading in bed | Evening use when white screens feel harsh

## Which one do you need?

- The lowest brightness still lights up the room: dimmer.

- White pages look harsh and blue in the evening: filter.

- Both: Night Light plus a dimmer with a black layer, or a dimmer with an amber or red tint like the filters here.

## A word on health claims

You will see a lot of claims online about blue light, melatonin and eye damage. I am not going to repeat them. Screen & Notification Dimmer is a comfort tool, not a medical device, and if you have eye pain or sleep problems a doctor is the right person to ask. What is simple and uncontroversial is that a darker, warmer screen is less disturbing in a dark room.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a blue light filter the same as dimming?

No. A filter changes colour, a dimmer changes brightness. Night Light alone will not take the screen below its minimum brightness.

### Should I use Night Light and a dimmer together?

Yes, if you want the screen both warmer and darker. Keep the dimmer's colour on Black so the tints don't double up.

# Overlay dimming vs real brightness: what actually happens

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
The system brightness slider changes how much light the panel produces. An overlay dimmer such as Screen & Notification Dimmer lays a semi-transparent dark layer over the image, so the screen looks darker even below the hardware minimum. On AMOLED screens darker pixels use less power, so an overlay can save a little battery. On LCD screens the backlight stays the same, so it does not. For the darkest, most efficient result, put the system slider at minimum first and then add the overlay.

## Two ways to make a screen darker

| | System brightness (backlight) | Overlay dimmer

| How it works | Lowers the panel's light output | Draws a dark, see-through layer over the image
| Lower limit | Set by the phone maker | Goes far below that
| Battery on LCD | Lower brightness saves power | Little or no saving; backlight unchanged
| Battery on AMOLED | Saves power | Darker pixels use less power, so a modest saving
| Contrast at very low levels | Good | Slightly reduced, as blacks and greys compress
| Appears in screenshots | No | Yes on most phones, so screenshots come out dark. Turn dimming off from the notification first

## Why the minimum is not lower

Phone makers choose the minimum so the screen stays readable in daylight and so the panel behaves well. On some OLED panels colours become uneven or blotchy at very low drive levels. That is part of why the minimum is higher than you might like at night, and why an overlay is the practical way to go further.

## PWM flicker

Many OLED phones dim by switching pixels on and off very quickly (PWM), often more slowly at low brightness. Some flicker-sensitive people therefore keep the system brightness higher and use an overlay to darken the picture. It is a known workaround, not a guaranteed fix, and how much it helps depends on the phone and the person.

## Best practice at night

- Turn on dark mode, so most apps are mostly black.

- Put the system brightness at its minimum (or use Extra dim, if you have it).

- Add the dimmer for the last step, and let the schedule do it for you every night.

- Turn on Auto-Dim if white pages still catch you out.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does a screen dimmer app save battery?

On AMOLED screens, a little, because darker pixels use less power. On LCD screens, hardly at all, because the backlight stays the same. Lowering the system brightness first saves the most.

### Is an overlay dimmer bad for an AMOLED screen?

No. It only changes what is displayed; darker pixels are, if anything, less wear.

### Do screen dimmer overlays show up in screenshots?

On most phones, yes. Android screenshots include overlays, so turn dimming off from the notification or tile before taking one.

## Related pages

- Screen dimmer app vs Android's Extra dim
- Screen Dimmer – OLED Saver vs Screen & Notification Dimmer
- Phone still too bright at its lowest brightness? 7 fixes

# Phone still too bright at its lowest brightness? 7 fixes

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
Phone makers set a minimum brightness that is meant for daylight, so in a dark room it can still feel harsh. Work through these in order: turn off adaptive brightness and drag the slider to zero, turn on dark mode, turn on Extra dim if your phone has it, add Night Light for warmth, then use a screen dimmer app such as Screen & Notification Dimmer to go below the minimum. A dimmer that also covers the notification shade fixes the last bright spot.

## 1. Drag the brightness slider fully left

Pull down Quick Settings and move brightness to the very bottom. If adaptive (auto) brightness is on, the phone may raise it again a moment later. Turn it off for the night, or simply drag it down once more, since adaptive brightness learns from your corrections.

## 2. Turn on dark mode

Settings > Display > Dark theme. Most of the glare at night comes from white backgrounds, and dark mode removes a lot of them. On AMOLED screens it also saves battery.

## 3. Use Extra dim if your phone has it

Search Settings for "Extra dim" or "Reduce bright colours". It lowers the screen past the normal minimum at the system level, and you can add its Quick Settings tile. Not every phone has it. See Extra dim vs a dimmer app.

## 4. Add Night Light for warmth

Night Light (or Eye Comfort Shield, Reading mode and similar, depending on the brand) doesn't make the screen darker, but a warmer screen feels less harsh. Schedule it for sunset to sunrise.

## 5. Use a screen dimmer app to go below the minimum

This is the step that actually breaks through the floor. A dimmer app draws a dark layer over everything. In Screen & Notification Dimmer:

- Install it from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".

- Tap a quick level: 20, 40, 60 or 80. Start at 40, then go darker.

- Turn on the free bedtime schedule so it happens every night by itself.

## 6. Fix the bright notification shade

Once everything else is dark, the pulled-down shade becomes the brightest thing on the phone. Turn on Dim notification bar so the overlay covers the status bar, the shade and the keyboard too.

## 7. Stop sudden white pages

If a web page or video still flashes you, turn on Auto-Dim. It darkens the layer when the content turns bright.

Set up an escape first

Before you go very dark, turn on shake or Volume Up + Volume Down under Settings > Emergency escape. Then you can always get the screen back without seeing it. How emergency off works.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why is my phone so bright at night even on the lowest setting?

The minimum brightness is set so the screen stays readable in daylight. In a dark room that floor can still be too bright, which is why dimmer apps exist.

### How do I make my screen darker than the lowest brightness on Android?

Use Extra dim if your phone has it, and/or a screen dimmer app such as Screen & Notification Dimmer, which draws a dark layer over the screen.

### Is it safe to make the screen that dark?

Yes. Screen & Notification Dimmer caps the layer at 97% so the screen never goes fully black, and you can turn it off by shaking the phone or pressing both volume buttons if you enable those.

- Dim below minimum brightness
- Screen dimmer app vs Android's Extra dim
- Dim the notification bar, status bar and keyboard on Android
- Emergency off: getting your screen back when it is too dark

# Using your phone in bed without waking anyone

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
To use your phone next to a sleeping partner or baby, take away the light first and the sound second. Dim the screen below its minimum with a dimmer such as Screen & Notification Dimmer (40 to 80 is usually enough), make sure the notification shade is dimmed too, turn the screen away from them, and switch on Do Not Disturb. A bedtime schedule makes all of this automatic.

Light is what wakes people. A phone at minimum brightness can still throw a surprising glow onto a white ceiling or a pillow, especially when a white web page opens. Here is the setup I recommend, in the order that makes the most difference.

## The setup

- Dark mode on, so most apps are mostly black.

- Brightness at minimum, adaptive brightness off.

- Dimmer at 40–80. In Screen & Notification Dimmer, the free bedtime schedule switches it on at 10:30 PM by default.

- Dim the notification shade, the single brightest thing left. How.

- Auto-Dim on if you browse, so white pages don't light up the room. How.

- Do Not Disturb and vibration off, so nothing buzzes on the bedside table.

- Tilt the screen away from them, and hold the phone lower, closer to your chest.

## Night feeds and checking on a baby

For a night feed, use Dim for with 30 or 60 minutes, so the phone goes back to normal afterwards without you thinking about it. The red night light filter keeps the room as dark as possible if you need to glance at the screen often.

## A table of starting levels

| Situation | Starting level

| Reading in bed, lamp off | 40
| Partner asleep beside you | 60
| Baby in the room | 60–80, red filter
| Very dark room, OLED phone | 80

Every panel is different, so treat these as starting points and adjust with the notification's −10 and +10 buttons.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I stop my phone screen waking my partner?

Dim it below minimum brightness with a dimmer app, also dim the notification shade, use dark mode, and turn the screen away from them.

### What dimming level should I use in bed?

Start at 40 to 60 and adjust. In a very dark room, 80 is common on OLED phones.

# Watching videos and reels in a dark room

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer
Video is the hardest thing to dim at night, because brightness jumps from scene to scene and from reel to reel. On Android, set the system brightness low, give your video apps a darker per-app level in Screen & Notification Dimmer, and turn on Auto-Dim so a bright scene or white reel is dimmed as it appears. Keep the filter on Black so colours stay true.

## Why video is different

Reading apps have fairly steady brightness. Video does not: a dark scene followed by a snowy one, or a black reel followed by one filmed on a white wall. A level that is fine for one is far too bright for the next.

## Setup for video apps

- Per-app level: set YouTube, Instagram and your video player to around 60–70. Everything else stays at your usual level.

- Auto-Dim on, with Reaction speed on Medium. Fast can feel jumpy in films; Gentle may react too late for reels.

- Colour filter: Black. Tints change skin tones and the look of a film.

- Edge slider for quick fixes mid-film without pausing. How.

Streaming apps and Auto-Dim

Some streaming apps protect their video from screenshots. Auto-Dim measures brightness through Android's screenshot API, so it may not react inside those apps. Use a fixed per-app level for them instead.

## Full-screen video and the status bar

In full-screen video the status bar is hidden anyway, but swiping down for a notification mid-film shows the bright shade. Dim notification bar covers that.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I stop bright videos hurting my eyes at night?

Lower the system brightness, use a darker per-app level for video apps, and turn on Auto-Dim so bright scenes are dimmed as they appear.

### Can I dim YouTube more than other apps?

Yes. Per-app profiles in Screen & Notification Dimmer let YouTube have its own darker level.

- Per-app levels: each app keeps its own darkness
- Edge slider: change the darkness by sliding along the screen edge

# Why your screen dimmer turns off by itself, and how to fix it

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
A dimmer that switches off on its own is almost always the phone's battery manager closing it in the background. Fix it by setting the app's battery usage to Unrestricted, allowing Autostart on Xiaomi, Vivo, Oppo and Realme, and, on Samsung, keeping it out of Sleeping apps. Screen & Notification Dimmer has an "Is everything working?" page that checks these for you and links to the right screen.

Stock Android lets a foreground service with a visible notification keep running, and that is how a dimmer stays on. Several phone makers add their own, stricter battery managers on top, and those can stop the service anyway, especially overnight. The website dontkillmyapp.com tracks this brand by brand.

## First, use the built-in checker

Open Screen & Notification Dimmer and go to Settings > Is everything working?. It checks the overlay permission, notifications, the Accessibility service, battery optimisation and Battery Saver, and counts how often the service stopped unexpectedly this week. On brands known for strict battery managers it shows a tip such as "Xiaomi phones stop background apps harder than stock Android", with buttons for Allow autostart and Set battery to unrestricted.

## Settings by brand

| Brand | What to change

| Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO (HyperOS / MIUI) | Settings > Apps > Manage apps > Night mode: Autostart on; Battery saver: No restrictions; Other permissions: "Display pop-up windows while running in the background" allowed. Lock the app in Recents (pull its card down)
| Samsung (One UI) | Settings > Apps > Night mode > Battery: Unrestricted. Settings > Battery > Background usage limits: make sure it is not in Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps
| OnePlus (OxygenOS) | Settings > Apps > Night mode > Battery usage: allow background activity / Unrestricted
| Vivo, iQOO (Funtouch / OriginOS) | Settings > Battery > Background power consumption management: allow high background usage; Autostart on in i Manager
| Oppo, Realme (ColorOS / Realme UI) | Settings > Apps > Night mode > Battery usage: allow background activity and auto launch
| Pixel and stock Android | Settings > Apps > Night mode > App battery usage: Unrestricted

Menu names change between versions, so use the Settings search if a path doesn't match exactly.

## Other causes

- Battery Saver on: some phones close background apps harder while it is active.

- Emergency off triggered: if you enabled shake, a shake in a pocket switches dimming off. The app shows "Night mode turned off by emergency escape" when that happens. Make the shake firmer, or use the volume buttons instead.

- Restarted phone: dimming doesn't come back after a reboot unless keep-after-restart (Pro) is on. The schedule does re-arm itself after a restart.

- A timer ran out: if you used Dim for, it turns off on purpose.

If the app does stop unexpectedly, it shows "Dimming stopped. Tap to restore." when you next open it.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why does my screen dimmer keep turning off?

Usually the phone's battery manager closes it. Set the app's battery usage to Unrestricted and, on Xiaomi, Vivo, Oppo and Realme, allow Autostart.

### Why does my dimmer stop on Xiaomi?

HyperOS and MIUI stop background apps aggressively. Allow Autostart, set Battery saver to No restrictions, and allow pop-up windows in Other permissions.

### Does the dimming schedule survive a restart?

Yes. The schedule re-arms itself after the phone boots. Restoring the current dimming after a restart needs keep-after-restart (Pro).

- A free bedtime schedule that dims the screen for you
- Emergency off: getting your screen back when it is too dark

# Free vs Pro, and unlocking Pro without paying

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 4 min read

Short answer
Screen & Notification Dimmer is free to use with no time limit: dimming below minimum brightness, the bedtime schedule, the timer, the notification buttons, the on/off tile and emergency off. Pro adds notification-bar dimming, the edge slider, Auto-Dim, per-app levels, colour filters, presets and keep-after-restart. You can buy Pro, or watch one short ad to unlock any single Pro feature for 12 hours. Watch three ads within 12 hours and all of Pro unlocks for 12 hours.

Ads only play when you tap that button yourself. There are no banner ads and no ads that pop up while you dim, read or watch. If you are in the EEA or UK, Google's consent form asks about ad personalisation first, and you can change your choice later in Settings.
