# Android screen dimmer: go below minimum brightness with an overlay

A 2026 guide to dimming an Android phone beyond its lowest brightness setting, and how Night Mode on Google Play does it.

## Quick answer

To make an Android screen darker than its minimum brightness, use an overlay dimmer app. Install Screen & Notification Dimmer on Google Play, allow “Display over other apps”, then pick a level such as 40 or drag the slider. The app draws a dark layer over the screen, so it goes darker than the brightness slider allows.

Get it on Google Play

## Why is the lowest brightness still too bright?

Phone makers set a minimum brightness so the screen stays readable in daylight. In a dark bedroom that floor can still feel harsh, especially when reading in bed or sitting next to someone who is asleep. The system brightness slider cannot go lower, which is where an overlay helps.

## How does an overlay screen dimmer work?

An overlay dimmer asks for Android’s “Display over other apps” permission and then draws a semi-transparent dark layer on top of the screen. Everything underneath, including apps, websites, video and the home screen, looks dimmer. Turning it off removes the layer straight away. Night Mode shows the level as a percentage darker than Android’s lowest brightness.

## Night Mode vs Extra dim, brightness, dark mode and blue light filters

These settings are often mixed up. They solve different problems.

| 
Method | What it does | Goes below minimum brightness?

| 
Brightness slider | Sets the display’s brightness within the range the phone allows | No

| 
Extra dim (built in) | A system setting on many phones that dims beyond the slider. Availability and strength depend on your phone and Android version | Yes, where available

| 
Night Light / blue light filter | Warms screen colours for the evening | No

| 
Dark mode | Switches supported apps to dark colours | No

| 
Night Mode app | Overlay dimmer with an adjustable level, free schedule, notification buttons and a Quick Settings tile; can also dim the notification shade (Pro) | Yes, you choose how far

Night Mode and Extra dim can be a good pair. If your phone has Extra dim, try both and keep whichever feels better.

## How to set up Night Mode on Android

- Install Screen Dimmer - Night Mode from Google Play and open it

- Allow “Display over other apps”. This is the only permission basic dimming needs. If Android shows “Screen overlay detected”, close other apps that draw over the screen and try again

- Choose a level. Tap 20, 40, 60 or 80, or drag the slider. Higher means darker than Android’s lowest brightness

- Adjust from anywhere. Use the notification buttons (−10, +10, OFF), the Quick Settings tile, or the Pro edge slider

See the User Guide for every control.

## What if it gets too dark?

- Shake the phone, if you turned it on in Settings > Emergency escape

- Tap OFF in the Night Mode notification, or use the Quick Settings tile

- Volume Up + Volume Down together, if you turned it on in Emergency escape (needs the optional Accessibility service)

Begin with 20 or 40 to get a feel for the levels, then go darker.

## Good to know

- The notification panel and status bar are dimmed only with Dim notification bar (Pro, or 12 hours with an ad) and the optional Accessibility service

- No account, and dimming works offline. Ads only play if you tap Watch an ad to unlock a Pro feature

- The bedtime schedule is free. Optional Pro adds notification-bar dimming, the edge slider, Auto-Dim, per-app levels and colour filters

- Night Mode is a screen dimmer, not a medical or eye-care device

If something is not working, see Troubleshooting.

# Frequently Asked Questions

## General

### What is Night Mode?

A screen dimmer for Android by Bunkwise Technologies (Google Play name: Screen & Notification Dimmer). It draws a dark layer over your display so you can dim the screen below your phone’s normal minimum brightness. There is no account.

### Which Android versions are supported?

Android 8.0 (Oreo) and newer. Auto-Dim needs Android 11 or newer. If your phone can install the app from Google Play, it is supported.

### Is there an iPhone version?

No. The phone app is Android only. A separate Night mode for Windows exists for PCs and laptops.

### Does dimming with an overlay damage my screen?

No. The dimming is a software layer drawn on top of what is on screen. Turning Night Mode off removes the layer straight away.

### Is Night Mode an eye-care or medical app?

No. It is a screen dimmer that helps you use your phone comfortably in the dark. It makes no medical claims and is not a medical device.

## Dimming

### Can Night Mode really make my screen darker than the lowest brightness setting?

Yes. Android’s brightness slider stops at a minimum that can still feel bright in a dark room. Night Mode’s overlay sits on top of that, so it can go further. The app shows the result as a percentage darker than Android’s lowest brightness.

### What do the 20, 40, 60 and 80 levels mean?

They are quick levels for how much darker than Android’s lowest brightness the screen should be. Start with 20 or 40 if you are new to the app, then go darker. You can also drag the slider to any value in between.

### How is Night Mode different from Android’s built-in Extra dim?

Extra dim is a system setting on many phones. Whether you have it, and how strong it is, depends on your phone and Android version. Night Mode is a separate app with an adjustable level, a free schedule, notification buttons, an edge slider (Pro) and Quick Settings tiles. They can be used side by side, so try both and keep what feels better.

### Does Night Mode work with Android dark mode?

Yes. Dark mode changes the colours apps use. Night Mode lowers how bright the whole screen looks, including white apps and websites, so the two do different jobs.

### Will dimming my screen help me sleep better?

We can’t promise that. Lower brightness at night is more comfortable for many people, but Night Mode is not a medical product. Treat it as one small part of a wind-down routine.

## Controls

### How do I change the dimming level without opening the app?

Use the buttons in the Night Mode notification (−10, +10, OFF, and AUTO for Auto-Dim), the Night mode tile in Quick Settings, or, with Pro, the edge slider and the Night slider tile.

### How do I turn Night Mode off quickly?

Tap OFF in the notification, switch off the Quick Settings tile, If you turned them on in Settings > Emergency escape, shaking the phone or pressing Volume Up and Volume Down together also turns it off. Both are off by default.

## Permissions and privacy

### Why does Night Mode need “Display over other apps”?

That permission lets the app draw the dark layer over everything on screen. Without it, dimming cannot work.

### Is the Accessibility permission required?

No, it is optional. The dimmer runs on the overlay permission alone. If you turn Accessibility on, it adds dimming of the status bar and notification panel, the volume-button emergency shortcut, per-app levels and Auto-Dim.

### Does Night Mode need an account?

No. There is no sign-up or login.

### What data does Night Mode collect?

Night Mode never asks for your name, email or contacts, and your settings stay on your phone. It includes Google AdMob (optional rewarded ads), Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics, and Microsoft Clarity, which collect device and usage data such as app screens opened and crash reports, subject to your consent where required. Purchases are handled by Google Play. See the Privacy Policy.

### Are there ads?

Only if you choose to watch one. Tapping Watch an ad on a locked Pro feature plays a short ad and unlocks that feature for 12 hours. Ads never appear by themselves, and Pro has none.

## Pro

### Is Night Mode free?

Yes. The core dimmer is free to use. The bedtime schedule and timer are free too. Optional Pro, a weekly subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase on Google Play (priced by country; see Free vs Pro), adds extra features, and each one can also be unlocked for 12 hours with an ad.

### What does Pro include?

Dimming the notification bar, status bar and keyboard, the edge slider, Auto-Dim, per-app levels, colour filters, presets and keep-after-restart. The User Guide has a full comparison.

## Windows

### Is there a Windows version of Night Mode?

Yes. It is a separate, free, open-source tray app for Windows 10 and 11. See Night mode for Windows.

## Still stuck?

See Troubleshooting or email support@bunkwise.in.

# Troubleshooting

Fixes for the most common problems.

## The screen won’t dim

- Make sure Display over other apps is allowed for Night Mode: Android Settings → Apps → Night Mode → Display over other apps

- If you denied the permission once, open Night Mode and tap a level again so it asks for it

- Check that Night Mode is switched on and the level is above 0%

- On Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones, also allow Display pop-up window for Night Mode in the app’s permissions

## The screen is too dark to see

- Shake the phone - if you turned it on in Settings > Emergency escape (it is off by default)

- Open the notification panel and tap OFF

- Switch off the Night mode Quick Settings tile

- If you turned it on in Emergency escape, press Volume Up and Volume Down together

Next time, start from 20 or 40 and move up in small steps.

## The notification panel isn’t dimmed

Dimming the notification panel needs Dim notification bar switched on (Pro, or 12 hours free with one ad) and the optional Accessibility service. Tap the “allow Accessibility to dim this panel” prompt in the Night Mode notification and turn the service on. Everything else dims without it.

## “Screen overlay detected” when I grant a permission

Android blocks permission screens while another app is drawing over the display. Close apps that float over the screen (chat bubbles, other dimmers or colour filters, screen recorders), then open the permission screen again.

## Dimming turns off after a while or after a restart

- Keep the Night Mode notification enabled so Android does not stop it

- Turn off battery optimisation for Night Mode: Android Settings → Apps → Night Mode → Battery → Unrestricted (the wording differs by phone)

- Aggressive battery management, common on Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo, Realme and OnePlus phones, can stop background apps. Some of these phones also have an “autostart” permission to enable

- After a restart, open Night Mode once and turn dimming on again, or turn on Keep dimming after restart (Pro). The bedtime schedule re-arms itself after a restart. Brand-by-brand settings are in Why your screen dimmer turns off by itself

## The volume-button shortcut doesn’t work

The Volume Up + Volume Down shortcut is off by default. Turn it on in Night Mode under Settings → Emergency escape, then allow the optional Accessibility service: Android Settings → Accessibility → Downloaded apps → Night mode - better dimming. Shaking the phone and the notification OFF button work without it.

## My Pro purchase isn’t recognised

- Make sure you are signed in to Google Play with the same Google account you purchased with

- Close and reopen Night Mode

- If Pro still does not appear, email us with your order number from Google Play

## Still stuck?

Email support@bunkwise.in with:

- Your phone model and Android version

- What you expected and what happened instead

Last updated: 25 November 2026

# Why Screen & Notification Dimmer?

By Madhav Raj, who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer
Screen & Notification Dimmer is built around the parts of night-time phone use that ordinary dimmers miss. It can dim the notification shade, status bar and keyboard. You can change the darkness from the screen edge in any app. Auto-Dim catches bright pages, the bedtime schedule is free, and you can switch it off blind with the volume buttons. It is updated often; version 8.0.2 came out on 21 November 2026.

I'm Madhav Raj, and I build this app at Bunkwise Technologies in India. Here is the honest case for it, and where you might be better off with something else.

## Six things it does differently

- It dims the parts other dimmers leave bright. The status bar, the pulled-down notification shade, Quick Settings, the keyboard and the lock screen. That is where the name comes from. How.

- The edge slider. Slide along the screen edge to change the darkness inside any app, like a volume bar. I didn't find this in the other dimmers I compared. How.

- Auto-Dim follows the content. It reacts when a white page opens, which a light sensor can't see in a dark room. How.

- The schedule is free. Several popular dimmers charge for it. How.

- You can't get stuck in the dark. Volume Up + Volume Down or a shake turns it off without looking, and the layer is capped at 97%. How.

- Pro without paying. One ad unlocks any Pro feature for 12 hours, and ads never appear on their own. How.

## Actively maintained

Android changes the rules for overlays, background services and notifications almost every year. Dimmers that aren't updated tend to break quietly on new phones. This app gets frequent updates (see What's new), targets the latest Android version (API 36), and includes a checker for the battery settings that break dimmers on Xiaomi, Samsung and other brands.

## Where other apps are better

- No ads at all: Penumbra has none and no paywall.

- Tasker automation: Penumbra and Twilight support it; I don't yet.

- Sunset-following blue light filter: Twilight.

- Root mode and customisable buttons: Darker.

- Track record: Night screen and Twilight have millions of users. This app is new, with 1K+ downloads so far.

## What users say

Two of the first Google Play reviews, both five stars, on version 6.1.0:

— Narayan, OnePlus Nord, Android 12, 11 October 2026

“Awesome”
— Trident, Redmi Note 13 5G, Android 15, 29 October 2026

That is a small sample. The app is new, so read the current reviews on Google Play too.

# Night mode for Windows

Free, open-source screen dimmer for Windows 10 and 11. It makes a laptop screen darker than its own lowest brightness. This is a separate app from the Android app.

Download for Windows (0.4 MB zip) Source on GitHub

## What is Night mode for Windows?

A free, open-source tray app. It first turns the real backlight down to the hardware minimum, then keeps dimming on screen down to 4% of normal brightness. Windows’ own brightness slider cannot go that low. It needs no account and shows no ads.

## How it dims

| 
Scale | What happens

| 
0–40 | The laptop’s real backlight goes down from your current level to the hardware minimum. This also saves battery

| 
40–100 | The sub-zero range: a full-screen colour filter dims the screen further, down to 4% of normal brightness. It is never fully black

- No backlight control: on a desktop or external monitor, the colour filter covers the whole scale instead

- Overlay method: if the colour filter is not available, or you choose Overlay in Settings, a click-through overlay is used instead

- Crashes: if the app crashes, Windows removes the filter, and the next launch restores your backlight

## Features

- Presets: Evening 30, Reading 50, Dark room 70, Pitch black 90, plus your own

- Colour: Natural, Warm (amber) or Grey

- Schedule, with a gradual ease-in

- App rules: dimming pauses while a chosen app is in front

- Full brightness for 30 seconds, 1 minute or 5 minutes, after which dimming comes back on its own

- Remember after restart and Start with Windows (both off by default)

## Install

- Download NightMode-1.1.1-win-x64.zip (0.4 MB) from the official GitHub release

- Unzip it: right-click the zip, choose Extract All…, then Extract. You can move the folder anywhere

- Run NightMode.exe. If Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”, click More info, then Run anyway. This happens because the app is new and not code-signed yet, and Windows asks only once

- Find it in the tray: Night mode lives next to the clock. If you do not see the moon icon, click the ^ arrow, then click the icon to open the panel

- Optional: open Settings → Dimming → Start with Windows so it is ready every time you sign in

To uninstall, quit the app from its tray menu and delete the folder. Settings are stored in %APPDATA%\NightMode, which you can delete too.

### Verify your download

Version 1.1.1, released 11 October 2026. SHA-256 of the zip:

a69e507349990bdf8c2962721a642f21d8364b8ec0ab216a61c4f2ca42f96ea0

Check it in PowerShell with Get-FileHash .\NightMode-1.1.1-win-x64.zip.

## Keyboard shortcuts

| 
Keys | Action

| 
Ctrl Alt D | Turn dimming on or off

| 
Ctrl Alt − / + | Darker or brighter, 5% at a time

| 
Ctrl Alt S | Take a screenshot at normal brightness

| 
Ctrl Alt Backspace | Full brightness right away, even if you cannot see the screen

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, with .NET Framework 4.8 (built into Windows 10 May 2019 Update and later; on an older Windows 10 install .NET Framework 4.8 first)

- Backlight control needs a laptop or another panel Windows can dim. On other screens, the colour filter does all the dimming

## Privacy

Night mode for Windows works fully offline. It has no account, no ads and no analytics, and it makes no network connections. Settings stay on your PC in a small JSON file.

## Windows FAQ

### Is Night mode for Windows free and open source?

Yes. It is free under the MIT licence, and the full C# source is at github.com/madhavraj840/bunkwise-night.

### Why does Windows say “Windows protected your PC”?

Microsoft Defender SmartScreen shows this for new apps that are not code-signed yet. Click More info, then Run anyway. The source is public and the SHA-256 checksum above lets you confirm the file.

### Is it better than the Windows Night light setting?

They do different jobs. Night light only warms colours. Night mode lowers brightness below the laptop minimum, and its Warm option can add an amber tint at the same time.

### Do screenshots come out dark?

Press Ctrl Alt S for a screenshot at normal brightness. Night mode lifts the filter, opens the Windows snipping tool and dims again afterwards.

## Build from source

You need the .NET SDK and the .NET Framework 4.8 Developer Pack. The app has no NuGet packages.

git clone https://github.com/madhavraj840/bunkwise-night
cd bunkwise-night
dotnet run --project checks
dotnet build NightMode.csproj -c Release -p:DebugType=none

# Privacy Policy

How Night Mode handles your data.

## Privacy at a glance

- No account. There is no sign-up or login

- Ads only if you choose. A short rewarded ad plays only when you tap Watch an ad to unlock a Pro feature. Pro has no ads

- No personal details asked for. Your settings stay on your phone and dimming works offline. The app includes Google AdMob, Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics, and Microsoft Clarity, which collect device and usage data (for example screens opened and crash reports), subject to your consent where required

- Payments for optional Pro are handled by Google Play

- Permissions: “Display over other apps” is required to draw the dimming layer. Accessibility is optional and only adds dimming of the status bar and notification panel, the volume-button shortcut, per-app levels and Auto-Dim

## Full policy

The complete, legally binding Night Mode privacy policy is published at bunkwise.in/privacypolicynightmode.html. If anything on this page differs from that policy, the full policy applies.

## Windows app

Night mode for Windows works fully offline, makes no network connections and has no account, ads or analytics. Settings stay on your PC.

## This website

This documentation site may use analytics to count visits. You can change your choice any time with Cookie settings in the page footer. See the website privacy page.

## Contact

Questions about privacy? Email support@bunkwise.in.

# Terms of Service

Terms for using Night Mode.

## Using Night Mode

Night Mode (“Screen Dimmer - Night Mode”) is provided by Bunkwise Technologies. By installing or using the app you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please uninstall the app.

## Free use and Pro

The core dimmer is free. Optional Pro features are sold through Google Play and are subject to Google Play’s payment, refund and subscription terms. Purchases are tied to your Google account.

## Safe use

- Night Mode makes your screen darker. Do not use it in situations where you need to see the screen clearly, such as while driving

- If the screen becomes too dark, use Emergency off: shake the phone, tap OFF in the notification, or switch off the Quick Settings tile

- Night Mode is a screen dimmer. It is not a medical device and makes no medical claims

## Permissions

Night Mode needs Display over other apps to work. The Accessibility service is optional and is used only for the features described in the User Guide. You can revoke either permission at any time in Android settings.

## No warranty

The app is provided “as is”, without warranties of any kind. Dimming appearance depends on your phone, its screen and its Android version, so results can vary.

## Limitation of liability

To the extent permitted by law, Bunkwise Technologies is not liable for indirect or consequential loss arising from the use of the app.

## Windows app

Night mode for Windows is open source and released under the MIT licence.

## Changes and contact

We may update these terms from time to time. The latest version is always on this page. Questions? Email support@bunkwise.in.
